rv.q: Mischief’s work is inspired by Michael Frayn’s masterpiece Noises Off and the rising farcical stakes of the first act bear a resemblance. But although this comedy is neatly plotted – with all balls thrown in the air eventually retrieved – there’s more going round in circles than cleverly building to...
If you are new to their style, it’s a fabulous introduction.
Every possible source of humour is mined good and hard and yet it feels that - with the exception of the opening sequence - no barrels are being scraped.
Mischief Comedy’s latest theatrical assault on the funny bone is riotously entertaining, breathtakingly well executed and, quite simply, one of the funniest shows I have seen in a very long time.
If you’re looking for a brilliant night out and a show that delivers plenty of laughs, About Spies is an easy recommendation.
The scriptwriting, the set design, the acting, everything comes together to produce an excellent comedy with great twists at the end.
Mischief fans and newbies alike will find plenty to enjoy here and will undoubtably refer to this as one of the company's greatest shows to date.
It genuinely is one of the most amusing shows to infiltrate the West End in years.
With its sharpened script, superb cast and relentless silliness, About Spies proves this is a spy mission well worth revisiting.
This gloriously British romp will have you laughing so hard you’ll blow your cover.
If you are looking for pure, unadulterated escapism, About Spies certainly delivers on laughs.
The second act is where the pace begins to drift.

cn.t: Mischief Theatre's Cold War spy spoof delivers their signature slapstick formula with gloriously silly results. Critics largely embrace the relentless farce and expert timing, though some find it repetitive and circular.
